Site-specific lead compounds representing the corresponding local coal environments were constructed, and Laplacian bond order (LBO) was used to identify preferred activation sites. Density functional theory calculations characterized the elementary reaction pathways, with transition states verified by intrinsic reaction coordinate analysis where applicable. LBO identified distinct activation centers for each functionality, while the three supply pathways exhibited closely convergent propagation barriers of 16.84, 17.71, and 17.68 kcal/mol, indicating concurrent operation with contributions governed primarily by functional-group abundance rather than strong kinetic selectivity. Peroxide homolysis acts as a kinetic gate at 33.50 kcal/mol, whereas carbonyl formation is facile and decarbonylation constitutes the downstream bottleneck at 22.47 kcal/mol. This network architecture predicts that carbonyl species should accumulate before substantial CO release. In-situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) and TG-MS confirm this prediction, showing carbonyl accumulation preceding the staged evolution of H2O, CO, and CO2. These results establish carbonyl as a key structural reservoir linking low-temperature oxidation chemistry to gas evolution and provide a mechanistic basis for interpreting gas-based indicators of coal spontaneous combustion.
items.authors: Yaqing Li, Tingting Huang, Jun Deng, Yutao Zhang, Seyed Borhan Mousavi, Saeed Zeinali Heris

items.title: From Computational Chemistry to Generative Models: A Survey of AI-Driven Small-Molecule Drug Discovery
items.abstract: Small-molecule drug discovery requires navigating enormous chemical space to identify candidates that are simultaneously potent, selective, synthetically accessible, and acceptable across pharmacokinetic and safety profiles; modern generative AI extends a long computational medicinal chemistry lineage that began with QSAR, pharmacophore modeling, and early structure-based de novo design. This survey focuses primarily on developments from 2017 to 2025, with the literature updated through 31 January 2026. Using a medicinal-chemistry lens, it first establishes the shared machinery of the field: molecular representations such as SMILES, SELFIES, graphs, fingerprints, three-dimensional coordinates, voxels, and latent vectors; commonly used datasets and benchmarks; and graph neural network encoders, including message-passing, directional, and equivariant architectures. We compare five principal generative mechanisms—autoregressive models, variational autoencoders, generative adversarial networks, normalizing flows, and diffusion models—together with reinforcement learning as a major goal-directed optimization framework. Across these approaches, we show that current methods offer complementary rather than interchangeable trade-offs, and we highlight recurring challenges, including validity versus synthesizability, limited prospective experimental validation, mode collapse and diversity loss, stereochemical and physical realism in three-dimensional design, computational cost, data scarcity, and the emerging convergence toward scaffold-conditioned generation, hybrid architectures, developability-aware optimization, and molecular foundation models.
items.authors: Houman Kazemzadeh, Kiarash Mokhtari, Seyed Reza Tavakoli, Nazanin Mirzaei, Ali Reza Keivanimehr, Shayan Majidifar

items.title: Unexpected effects of the addition of copper(II) bisphenanthroline complexes in Chan-Lam couplings
items.abstract: The effect of the addition of bis(2,9-dimethyl-1,10-phenanthroline)copper(II) chloride and bis(1,10-phenanthroline)copper(II) chloride on Chan-Lam couplings with copper acetate and a previously reported coordination complex LCuCl were investigated with respect to their potential role as redox shuttles in the catalytic cycle. In neither case action as a redox shuttle was observed. While no effects were observed in reactions catalysed by LCuCl, addition to reactions catalyzed by copper acetate gave more complicated results, sometimes with drastically increased activity. Detailed investigations found that (i) ligand exchange results in the formation of a more active mono-phenanthroline copper complex and (ii) formation of mixed chloride/acetate salts lead to significant increases in activity. This result could not be generalized for a wider range of N-nucleophiles or observed for anion combinations other than chloride/acetate.
items.authors: Émile Frappier, Frank Schaper

items.title: Mild Organic Acid Induced Acidochromism of Spiropyran
items.abstract: Mild organic acid induced acidochromic transformation of spiropyran is presented herein. Benzoic acids bearing electron-withdrawing substituents efficiently induced the acidochromic transformation of spiropyran, which was monitored using UV–visible and NMR spectroscopy. Kinetic studies revealed a zero-order dependence of the reaction rate on the concentration of benzoic acids. Furthermore, control experiments and DFT calculations demonstrated the pivotal role of the methoxy (–OMe) substituent on the spiropyran core, which facilitates acidochromism by bringing organic acids into close proximity via hydrogen-bonding interactions. Furthermore, biologically relevant acids, including citric acid and tartaric acid, were also found to effectively induce the acidochromic transformation.
items.authors: Sonalin Senapati, Manoranjan Ojha, Suranjan De, Sandeepan Maity

items.title: AQ-GNoME: an Aqueous Stability Augmentation of the GNoME Database
items.abstract: Aqueous stability is a fundamental requirement for materials used in electrochemical energy technologies, yet no systematic Pourbaix stability screening has been performed for Google DeepMind’s GNoME database of more than 520,000 novel inorganic crystals. Here, we introduce AQ-GNoME, an aqueous-stability augmentation of the GNoME database, enabling systematic shortlisting of GNoME candidates for electrochemical applications. The database additionally includes machine-learning-based substitutional-disorder predictions and Herfindahl–Hirschman Index supply-risk metrics, thereby supporting structural-order and supply-risk based filtering. User-defined criteria across electrochemical potential and pH, elemental composition, structural order, and supply concentration reduce the database to a manageable, project-specific shortlist. We apply AQ-GNoME to identify GNoME materials relevant for further investigation in electrochemical CO2 reduction (eCO2RR) and acidic oxygen evolution (OER), focusing on candidates absent from the Materials Project and ICSD. For eCO2RR, combining aqueous stability criteria with a compositional heuristic intended to mimic copper’s selectivity, we identify 8 ordered multimetallic candidates. For acidic OER, combining stability and supply-concentration criteria, we identify 39 Ir-lean oxides, of which 26 are metallic under HSE06 DFT. AQ-GNoME therefore provides a practical framework for electrochemical materials discovery within GNoME, reducing the search space from more than half a million compounds to experimentally tractable candidate sets.
items.authors: Mathias S. Nissen, Peter Beck, Leo Karlsson, Manuel Dillenz, Alexander Bagger, Ivano E. Castelli

items.title: Per-Stage Controls and Failure Modes in a Co-Folding Virtual Screening Cascade for the Keap1–Nrf2 Interaction
items.abstract: Virtual-screening cascades assembled from co-folding and learned-affinity models are now routine, and each stage is usually trusted on the strength of its own score. We measured, stage by stage, whether those scores carry the information a practitioner would attribute to them, using the Keap1–Nrf2 protein–protein interaction and a 130,793-compound make-on-demand library as the test bed. Most measurements are negative, and none of the failure modes is specific to one of the two models tested. Two independently developed affinity models order activity-cliff pairs above chance (about 68% of 181 pairs) but carry no information about the size of the potency gap, and both couple to molecular weight; the built-in molecular-weight correction rescales without de-biasing. Neither model resolves enantiomers, including the model that generates an explicit high-confidence three-dimensional pose. Pose-model confidence is only weakly informative about geometric validity, so an explicit validity check is required rather than optional. Training-free guidance is required for stereochemical fidelity in pose generation, and diffusion steps can be halved without detectable loss. A seeded matched-decoy gate validates the pose-and-energy stage where no single physicochemical descriptor does, and the pose model reproduces all five co-crystal references below 2 Å, three of them released after its training cutoff. Single-structure MM-GBSA ordering is not validated by ensemble refinement, and the two solvation models disagree both on the ordering and on which candidates are separable at all. The control suite is released as a reusable artifact.
items.authors: Huynh-Duc Le

items.title: Cumulative Charge as a Workload-Aware Comparison Coordinate for Pulsed High-Current OER Stability
items.abstract: The interpretation of electrode degradation under dynamic electrolysis is complicated by the fact that degradation rates expressed per unit time depend not only on the degradation response but also on the electrochemical workload imposed during the test. Here, we investigate this effect for porous NiFe OER electrodes operated in an alkaline gas-diffusion-electrode half-cell configuration under pulsed galvanostatic operation at 1-3 A·cm-2. Two pulse protocols, corresponding to 86% and 96% active operation time, were evaluated using 36 electrode tests from two independent deposition batches. Degradation was quantified both per unit elapsed time and per cumulative areal charge using iR-corrected electrode potentials, sample-level regression, random-effects pooling, and batch-aware statistical analysis. In the time domain, the degradation rate increased substantially with current density, from 19.2 ± 4.7 to 53.4 ± 23.6 mV·h-1 for the 86% active-operation protocol. In contrast, the charge-normalized voltage loss remained approximately constant at 5.6-6.2 mV·(kC·cm-2)-1 over 1-3 A·cm-2 for the same protocol. The 96% protocol showed a similar overall reduction in apparent current-density dependence after charge normalization, although the 2 A·cm-2 condition exhibited a distinct deviation. Furthermore, at 3 A·cm-2, increased non-linearity, signal variability, and post-electrolysis structural damage indicated a transition to a failure-prone operating regime in which linear charge-normalized degradation was no longer sufficient to describe electrode behavior. Our results demonstrate that elapsed-time degradation rates can overstate apparent current-density and duty-cycle effects during pulsed high-current electrolysis. The charge-normalized voltage loss therefore provides a useful workload-aware descriptor for comparing degradation within the stable operating regime, while high-current failure processes require separate consideration.
items.authors: Oleg I. Zaitsev, Etienne Berner, Gustav K.H. Wiberg, Matthias Arenz

items.title: Bottom-up design of the operating window for direct urea synthesis from first-principles molecular thermodynamics
items.abstract: Urea, among the most widely utilized foods for crops, is mass-produced via the carbon-and energy-intensive Bosch–Meiser process. However, its operating condition is settled empirically, vulnerable to undersampling and suboptimal production, and its molecular mechanism is not well understood. Here we present a bottom-up design of the operating condition driven by first-principles molecular modeling. Using a machine learning force field trained on first-principles calculations of urea and relevant species, we explored the free energy surface of the reaction space from reactant to product across temperatures. We found a strong thermodynamic preference for acyl substitution over competing pathways, with a free energy minimum around 420 K arising from the balance between carbamic acid’s protonation ratio and solvation number, which respectively increase and decrease with temperature. And we confirmed that the optimal condition originates from near-critical behavior, showing a fixed ratio to the critical temperature below unity. The maximum-yield temperatures of simulation and experiment correspond when scaled to their critical temperatures, suggesting this combined approach for engineering the operating condition.
items.authors: Minwoo Kim, Seungtae Kim, Ji Woong Yu, Won Bo Lee

items.title: From Static Material Design to Predictive Open-Loop Control via Chemistry–Architecture Coupling in a Moving-Boundary Reaction–Diffusion Framework
items.abstract: Bioactive silicate ceramics, wollastonite (CaSiO3), diopside (CaMgSi2O6), and apatite–wollastonite glassceramics constitute a unique class of bone-regeneration materials whose therapeutic action is intrinsically coupled to their own degradation. Yet the field continues to design these materials as static objects, optimizing initial composition, porosity and elastic modulus while evaluating outcomes at fixed endpoints, tacitly ignoring the central fact that the physicochemical microenvironment they create evolves continuously and irreversibly. We argue that this temporal evolution is not a side effect but the therapeutic mechanism itself, and that it can be engineered predictively. This review consolidates and mathematically hardens the emerging paradigm of spatiotemporal trajectory engineering: the pre-encoded, open-loop programming of a degrading scaffold’s full physicochemical trajectory through coupled control of ceramic network chemistry and pore-network architecture. Three advances over prior treatments are delivered. First, the solid-state chemistry foundation is deepened: Qn speciation from 29Si MAS-NMR is mapped onto hydration versus hydrolysis activation barriers; the incongruent dissolution cascade (cation exchange → silica-gel layer → hydroxycarbonate apatite nucleation) is formalized as a coupled surface–gel-layer–precipitation problem; and the autocatalytic OH−-feedback loop that drives local pH spikes is quantified, together with surface-specific XPS O 1s BO/NBO deconvolution as the front-tracking metric. Second, the static reaction–diffusion model is upgraded to a moving-boundary erosion formulation: an explicit porosity-evolution law, a dynamically self-consistent effective diffusivity, and interstitial convective (Brinkman) transport are introduced, yielding a two-dimensional Damköhler–Péclet regime map that delineates four phenomenologically distinct trajectory regimes, reaction-limited, diffusion-limited, convective washout, and convection-amplified dosing, plus a coupled design corridor where trajectory classes diverge maximally. Third, biological admissibility is replaced from discrete endpoint thresholds to a continuous phase-indexed Regenerative Target Zone (RTZ) envelope incorporating M1-gating, M2-switch, and HCA-maturation kinetics; and the computational pipeline is extended with functional data analysis (fPCA, DTW), neural ordinary differential equations, physicsinformed neural networks, Hamiltonian Monte Carlo credible tubes, and Bayesian-optimal experimental design. The resulting framework is fully specified, falsifiable, and implementable with open-source tools and standard instrumentation. It reclassifies the design problem from optimizing a material to programming an evolving microenvironment, and because the temporal program is pre-encoded without biological sensing, it qualifies as a passive implant under current regulatory frameworks.
items.authors: Andualem Belachew Workie

items.title: Globally Aromatic 10-Boratetraoxacorroles: Boron-Doped Macrocyclic Chromophores with Intense Red-to-Near-Infrared Emission
items.abstract: Neutral, globally aromatic boron-containing macrocycles are exceptionally rare, with the 10-bora-21,22,23,24-tetraoxacorroles reported herein representing only the second class of such compounds known to date, following the 5-bora-21,22-dioxaporphyrin we recently described, and are also the first neutral, globally aromatic boracorroles. Here, we present a furan-based 10-bora-21,22,23,24-tetraoxacorrole and an oxadiborepin-fused derivative thereof. The global aromaticity of both macrocyclic boranes in the neutral state is supported by experimental data and NICS and ACID cal­culations. They exhibit intense absorption spanning the ultraviolet to near-infrared (NIR) regions of the electromagnetic spectrum. Notably, the novel boracorroles display bright red and red-to-NIR fluorescence, achiev­ing quantum yields more than twice (Φ fl = 35–46%) that of conventional triphenylcorrole (Φ fl = 19%). DFT analysis reveals that the frontier orbital en­ergies are strongly modulated by the meso- B atom, generating a large HOMO to HOMO−1 energy gap and, consequently, mark­edly enhanced Q-band extinction coefficients arising from the predominantly single-configurational character of the S 0 →S 1 transition (HOMO to LUMO). Incorporation of the BOB bridge in the oxadiborepin-fused derivative significantly stabilizes the LUMO, giving rise to red-shifted absorption and emission alongside distinct electrochemical behavior. In addition, the BOB unit further amplifies the global aromaticity of the boracorrole, underscoring efficient π-conjugation across this heteroatomic bridge.
items.authors: Jonas Fehler, Lukas Swoboda, Alexandra Friedrich, Vivien Schütz, Holger Helten

items.title: Polymer Informatics Atlas: Property-Specific Representations, Chemistry-Aware Generalization, and Reliability-Aware Machine Learning Across Five Polymer Properties
items.abstract: Polymer-property machine learning is often evaluated as if representation choice, random-split accuracy, chemical extrapolation, transfer learning, uncertainty, and chemical interpretation were a single problem. Here, these questions are separated in a six-stage Polymer Informatics Atlas built from 7,973 unique RDKit-valid polymer repeat units in the NeurIPS Open Polymer Prediction 2025 dataset. Thirty-six interpretable composition/structure descriptors and radius-4, 2,048-dimensional count Morgan fingerprints were evaluated independently and as a hybrid representation for glass-transition temperature (Tg), fractional free volume (FFV), thermal conductivity (Tc), density, and radius of gyration (Rg). Frozen property-specific models achieved untouched random-holdout R2 values of 0.608, 0.704, 0.825, 0.920, and 0.703, respectively. However, chemistry-separated testing changed this interpretation substantially: Tc fell to R2 = 0.326, whereas density remained comparatively robust at R2 = 0.874. Representation-block permutation showed that density was predominantly captured by interpretable global chemistry, while Tc and Rg depended more strongly on local/topological structure; Tg and FFV required mixed information. Masked multitask learning on the overlapping Tc-Density-Rg block used incomplete labels more efficiently than complete-case training, but gains over matched single-task neural networks were small and seed dependent. Five-member ensembles combined with splitconformal calibration produced 90% nominal intervals with empirical coverages of 95.7% (Tc), 92.3% (density), and 98.5% (Rg). Finally, 28 predictive Morgan indices were decoded to atom-centred environments after exact fingerprint-regeneration audits, and an integrated descriptor/fingerprint manifold was used for chemical-space visualization, archetype selection, and an illustrative high-Tc/low-density Pareto analysis. The results support a property-specific, domain-aware view of polymer informatics in which predictive accuracy is reported together with chemical support, uncertainty, and explicit claim boundaries rather than as a single global score.
items.authors: Dennis Obinna Orji

items.title: Three-Component Alkene Difunctionalization Enabled by Continuous-Flow Generation of the NCF3 Anion
items.abstract: Multicomponent alkene difunctionalization provides an efficient route to molecular complexity by forging multiple bonds in a single operation. Although radical-polar crossover chemistry has greatly expanded the scope of these transformations, the use of highly reactive fluorinated nucleophiles remains largely unexplored because of their limited accessibility and poor stability. Here, we report the first three-component alkene difunctionalization employing the NCF3 anion as the nucleophilic reaction partner. The key to this transformation is the on-demand generation of the NCF3 anion in continuous flow, followed by its direct merger with visible-light photoredox catalysis. This strategy enables the coupling of a diverse range of radical precursors with styrenes and the flow-generated NCF3 anion through the sequential combination of radical and polar reactivities under mild photochemical conditions. The protocol accommodates extensive variation of the radical precursor, the alkene component and the NCF3 anion itself, and is applicable to the late-stage diversification of pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals. More broadly, this work demonstrates how continuous-flow generation of reactive intermediates can unlock multicomponent reaction manifolds that remain inaccessible using conventional batch methods.
items.authors: Dmitrii Nagornîi, Maria Teresa Tiberi, Mattia Lepori, Nikolaos Kaplaneris, Tom Roberts, Sebastian C. Cosgrove

items.title: Sustainable time-temperature integrator for perishable fresh foods based on polymer/graphene blends
items.abstract: Monitoring the thermal history of perishable food products along the cold chain is critical to guarantee quality and safety for consumers. Time-temperature integrators (TTIs) offer solutions to guarantee cold chain efficiency, improve safety, and reduce food waste. Here, we present a sustainable TTI device based on the irreversible dehydration of a hydrogel, made of reduced graphene oxide and PEDOT:PSS, when exposed to varying environmental conditions. Dehydration kinetics of the hydrogel are investigated over a range of temperatures and relative humidity relevant to food-storage applications. The TTI response is quantified by the mass loss evolution which is interpreted by means of a kinetic model leveraging the initial hydrogel mass, the temperature and the relative humidity. The Arrhenius-like energy barrier is greater than the water binding enthalpy within the hydrogel, and the dehydration rate of the TTI device is finely tuned through the initial mass to mimic the microbial growth curve on fresh sea bream fillet. Deviations of the TTI from its evolution upon optimum conditions reveal the occurrence of a breach in the cold chain. We demonstrate that it is possible to translate the TTI assessment on a smartphone by imaging the evolution of shrinking of the projected area.
items.authors: Mattia Bosi, Matteo Sensi, Alessandro Paradisi, Marcello Berto, Evgenia Basdeki, Emmanouil Flemetakis

items.title: IntegroPectin in aqueous solution: a multi-scale computational investigation of solvation, conformational dynamics, and thermodynamic partitioning of a naringeningalacturonic acid–rhamnose glycoconjugate
items.abstract: A novel class of flavonoid-pectin bioconjugates sourced via cavitation of citrus processing waste, citrus IntegroPectin pectic polymers exhibit a complex structural synergy between the pectic backbone and co-extracted flavonoids imparting these biopolymers with broad scope biological activity. Using a reductionist approach, we explore the hydration behavior of Model A — a neutral naringenin-esterified disaccharide (GalA(1→2)Rha) modeling the structure of grapefruit IntegroPectin via a multiscale computational workflow spanning isolated-molecule DFT, topological analyses, mixed implicit–explicit iterative micro-solvation, explicitsolvent molecular dynamics, and continuum thermodynamics. The solvation of Model A (naringenin–galacturonic acid–rhamnose) is governed by a rigid, preorganized conformation in which the most electrostatically attractive sites are topologically saturated by intramolecular hydrogen bonds. Water therefore occupies a hierarchy of available rather than optimal sites, forming an anisotropic percolating network whose electronic, geometric, topological, and spectroscopic signatures are mutually consistent across four levels of theory and three timescales. Analysis points to a genuine decoupling between the spatial and electronic descriptions of hydration that neither a purely energetic nor a purely geometric analysis could reveal alone.
items.authors: Nicolas Michel, Anne-Sylvie Fabiano-Tixier, Rosaria Ciriminna, Giovanna Li Petri, Giuseppe Angellotti, Mario Pagliaro

items.title: Azopyrazole boronic ester crosslinks with long thermal half-lives for phototunable viscoelastic hydrogels
items.abstract: Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) based on boronic acid–ester exchange undergo rapid network reconfiguration in ambient conditions, making them useful materials for biomedical applications. The combination of photoswitches and dynamic bonds imparts reversible spatiotemporal control over mechanical properties for smart and responsive materials. Here, we report azopyrazole boronic acids that undergo rapid photoisomerization to their metastable Z isomers, which have extremely long thermal half-lives (over a year at 25 °C) and a 3-fold enhancement in binding affinity for diols compared to the E isomer. When incorporated into hydrogels, these photoswitchable dynamic bonds enable reversible changes in stiffness and stress relaxation time with at least 6 cycles of visible and UV light. Despite only containing dynamic crosslinks, these hydrogels are comparable in stiffness to our previously reported hybrid materials containing dynamic azobenzene boronic ester and static bis(acrylamide) crosslinks. This work demonstrates an alternative strategy to tuning boronic acid-ester equilibria with light while maintaining strong binding in both isomers.
items.authors: Mara L. Paterson, Tomas Castillo, Sarah Lin, Julia A. Kalow

items.title: Computational Discovery and Characterization of Cancer-associated Variants in DNA Transaction Enzymes: Impact of a Glioma–associated mutation on Thymine-DNA Glycosylase
items.abstract: DNA transaction pathways play a fundamental role in maintaining genome integrity through the regulation of DNA replication, repair, recombination, and epigenetic modification. When these pathways are disrupted, it can lead to genomic instability and contribute to disease initiation and progression. Genome-wide association studies and follow–up analysis from data generated by these studies continue to identify numerous disease-associated variants, although functional characterization of missense mutations arising from these variants remains a challenge. In this study, we employed a hypothesis-driven computational framework to identify statistically significant cancer-associated variants in DNA transaction genes across four different cancer phenotypes using genome-wide association study databases. Bioinformatics analyses were used to prioritize missense variants based on their statistical significance. Among the identified variants, the thymine DNA glycosylase (TDG) missense variant rs4135113 was selected for detailed structural characterization because of the critical role of TDG in base excision repair and active DNA methylation. Classical molecular dynamics simulations were performed to investigate the impact of the resulting TDG variant on its structure and dynamics. In addition, the impact of biologically relevant post-translational modifications on both wild-type TDG and variant proteins were investigated. Our results uncover 74 previously unreported cancer–associated SNPS for the four tested phenotypes, including 7 pleiotropic variants. Additionally, our atomistic analysis of a glioma–associated TDG variant provides a detailed insights into how a cancer-associated variant in TDG may impact its function and highlight the importance of combining bioinformatics with molecular simulations to connect genetic data with underlying biological mechanisms.
items.authors: Upeksha C. Dissanayake, Architha Cunnapakkam, Ramya Konduru, G. Andrés Cisneros

items.title: Interfacial Chain Mobility in Polymer–Silica Elastomers Governs the Balance between Biocompatibility and Tissue-Like Mechanics
items.abstract: Soft biological tissues combine biocompatibility, viscoelastic energy dissipation and J-shaped nonlinear elasticity, yet the molecular principles for reproducing these properties in artificial soft materials remain unclear. Here we identify interfacial chain mobility, rather than interaction strength, as a key parameter governing tissue-like mechanics in composite elastomers. Using non-aggregated silica particles dispersed in biocompatible PMEA and PMEO2MA networks, we decouple polymer–particle interactions from filler aggregation. Strong multipoint interactions in PMEO2MA create a constrained interphase that suppresses chain mobility and promotes premature stiffening. By contrast, moderate PMEA–silica interactions preserve interfacial mobility while enabling efficient stress transfer. This balance produces J-shaped elasticity through finite chain extensibility and pronounced hysteresis through reversible interfacial stress transfer. Our results reveal complementary molecular origins of nonlinear elasticity and energy dissipation, establishing interfacial chain mobility as a design principle for biointegrated soft materials combining flexibility, damping, biocompatibility and tissue-like mechanical performance.
items.authors: Daiki Miyake, Karin Ito, Moeka Higuchi, Moe Sakamoto, Fumio Asai, Xiaobin Liang

items.title: Hydridoaluminastibanes: A New Class of Al–Sb Bonded Main-Group Compound
items.abstract: Reactions of an Al(I) center with Sb–Cl, Bi–Cl and, notably, Sb–H reagents afford a family of Al(III) complexes featuring structurally characterized, pnictogen–halide and –hydride bonds. The Sb–H reaction is particularly striking, simultaneously forging Al–Sb and Al–H bonds to give the first hydridoaluminastibane establishing the previously unknown Al(Sb)(H) functional group. These results introduce pnictogen hydride oxidative addition as a new strategy for Al–Sb bond formation and expands the reactivity landscape of hydrostibination.
items.authors: Elizabeth A. McKenzie, Gabriel J. Jobin, Mitchell A. MacEachern, A. Dina Dilinaer, Saurabh S. Chitnis, Marcus W. Drover

items.title: Unusual reactivities of “NONO” calix[4]arene aluminum complexes
items.abstract: Reaction of dibenzylaminocalix[4]arene, L1H2, with aluminum alkyls did not lead to deprotonation of both phenolic groups but provided aluminum or aluminate complexes containing phenolic OH or anilinium NH2 + groups in the presence of aluminum alkyl groups. Upon heating aluminum complexes L1AlMe and L1AlCl were obtained. Reaction of L1AlMe with amines led to amido complexes, either of the ancillary amine or the aniline moiety of L1. Further reaction with isopropanol yielded L1AlOiPr. Heating in the absence of amine afforded the phenyl complex L1AlC6D5 by activation of the NMR solvent. Reaction with two equivalents of AlMe3 led to -H abstraction from methyl to form methylene-bridged (L1-2H)(AlMe)2CH2. Reactions of bis(S,S-2-(dimethylamino)cyclohexyl)amino) calix[4]arene, L2H2, with AlEt2Cl or AlMe3 led directly to the anilido complex (L2-H)Al. Reaction with two equivalents of AlMe3 yielded (L2-2H)Al2CH2 after -H abstraction from methyl. Both compounds reacted with isopropanol to form L2AlOiPr. Isopropoxide complexes L1AlOiPr and L2AlOiPr were moderately active in lactide polymerization (yielding essentially atactic polylactide) and the Meerwein-Ponndorf-Verley reduction of benzophenone. Reaction of methylene-bridged (L2-2H)Al2CH2 with benzophenone afforded diphenylethylene in transition-metal-free methylenation.
items.authors: Matteo Cardoso, Victor Trudel-Lalande, Frank Schaper

items.title: Development of Efficient Blue OLEDs: A Systematic Investigation of the Effect of the Nature of the Host on Exciton Dynamics in Operating TADF Devices
items.abstract: The continuing demand for sharper and brighter displays is driving the development of efficient blue organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). However, achieving high maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE max ) and low efficiency roll-off is still a major challenge for blue-emitting devices. Herein, we report highly efficient blue multi-resonant thermally activated delayed fluorescent (MR-TADF) OLEDs showing EQE max of 32.5% and relatively moderate efficiency roll-off (EQE: 26.3% at 100 cd m -2 and 14.6% at 1000 cd m -2 ). Several host:emitter combinations were explored to correlate the nature of the emissive layer formulation to the 2 differences in device efficiencies. Here, the photophysical measurements did not adequately explain the differences in device performance; however, direct measurement of exciton dynamics in operating OLEDs and single-carrier devices revealed that charge accumulation at the interface between the transport layer and host resulted in increased exciton-polaron annihilation and the loss of efficiency. This highlights the importance of measurements on operating devices, as the differences in efficiency between devices could not be explained by conventional photophysics alone.
items.authors: Hassan Hafeez, Sen Wu, Liam King, Quan Qi, David B. Cordes, Eli Zysman-Colman

items.title: Toward Environmentally Stable Transition-Metal Dichalcogenides: Defect-Selective Docking of Au Nanoparticles on MoS2, MoSe2, and MoTe2
items.abstract: Defect sites in two-dimensional (2D) transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) can enhance surface reactivity and charge-transfer interactions, but the same exposed metal centers can accelerate degradation under environmental conditions. Selective functionalization of these sites therefore offers an opportunity to improve TMD stability without sacrificing the broader functionality of the 2D surface. Herein, we use density functional theory to examine Au 55 nanoparticle (NP) attachment to pristine and chalcogen-vacancy-containing MoS 2 , MoSe 2 , and MoTe 2 , with emphasis on the interplay between surface diffusion, NP capture, and interfacial bonding. Au 55 preferentially binds chalcogen vacancies across all three TMDs, supporting defect-directed nanoparticle functionalization as a route toward selective passivation. However, the specific surface behavior is strongly material dependent: vacancy binding is strongest for MoSe 2 , whereas surface diffusion is most facile on MoS 2 and vacancy docking is kinetically most accessible on MoTe 2 . Surface-diffusion barriers of 0.34, 0.38, and 0.46 eV are obtained for MoS 2 , MoSe 2 , and MoTe 2 , respectively, while the direct vacancy-docking barriers are 0.59, 0.68, and 0.31 eV. The resulting vacancy-bound complexes exhibit large detachment barriers, indicating stable localization under ambient conditions. Au decoration also produces distinct work-function and charge-transfer responses across the TMD series. These results demonstrate that defect-directed Au NP functionalization is potentially general across TMDs, while its effectiveness remains intrinsically material dependent. The distinct interplay of nanoparticle mobility, vacancy capture, interfacial bonding, and electronic response provides a basis for tailoring NP–TMD interfaces for applications that rely on controlled surface reactivity and charge transfer, including gas sensing, photocatalysis, and environmental contaminant conversion, while enhancing environmental stability.
items.authors: Maciej J. Szary

items.title: Active Confinement Catalysis Powered by Mechanical Force.
items.abstract: The design of artificial enzyme mimics has long been guided by the paradigm of crafting static pockets for transition-state stabilization, a process reliant on stochastic molecular diffusion. These passive events impose a rate limit, and a strict criterion for substrates with suitable size and electronic matching. Inspired by biological ion pumps that drive uphill ion transport using chemical fuels, we propose that mechanical force can power an active, out-of-equilibrium catalytic pumping cycle. We herein report a solid-state mechanochemical strategy where mechanical input drives a confinement catalyst 1 ( Pd 2 L 2 ) from a closed to an open “active” state, while simultaneously pumping substrate molecules into its active site for catalytic events. This dynamic catalyst exhibits substrate size and shape recognition, and its mechano-pump mechanism is quantitatively validated by Michaelis-Menten saturation kinetics, where catalytic efficiency scales directly with the applied force. Moreover, the active-pump action overcomes inherent electrostatic repulsion, enabling cationic substrates, normally excluded from the cationic host catalysts, to be efficiently drawn in and engaged in catalytic turnover. This force-induced pumping catalysis concept is smoothly extended to photochemistry. By combining a photosensitizing unit and an active confinement catalyst, an active pumping mechano-photoredox C-H oxidation process is developed. This work establishes mechanical force not merely as a synthetic tool, but as a fundamental design parameter for catalysts, opening a pathway to life-like chemical control in which energy transduction, not just static structure, dictates function.
items.authors: Shi Li, Fang-Zi Liu, Xinhan Liu, Yan Liu, Jian Wang, KaKing Yan

items.title: Regularized Alternatives to Conventional Density Fitting: Tikhonov Regularization with Discrete Picard Condition
items.abstract: Density fitting (DF) reduces the computational cost of correlated electronic-structure methods but can become unstable when the fitting metric contains small eigenvalues or near-linear dependencies. We introduce a set of protocols based on Tikhonov regularization (TR) combined with the Discrete Picard Condition (DPC) to adaptively determine an effective truncation of the auxiliary space in DF-MP2. Truncation indices are selected using either a two-line L-curve fit or local sharp-corner protocols. The TR-DPC approaches are evaluated against conventional DF-MP2 and Cholesky decomposition (CD) across the S22 benchmark set and an AlkB hydrogen-atom-transfer reaction. The three-point sharp-corner methods provide the best overall accuracy among the TR-DPC protocols, while the two-line method is less accurate but more robust for reduced or poorly matched auxiliary spaces. CD provides the closest agreement with conventional DF-MP2; however, for the systems examined here, it generates more Cholesky vectors than the number of functions in the corresponding DF auxiliary basis and is accompanied by greater computational cost. TR-DPC provides a useful alternative by reducing the effective auxiliary representation while maintaining small, often sub-kcal mol⁻¹, errors, providing a balance between accuracy, representation size, and computational cost.
items.authors: Jose P. Madriaga, G. Andrés Cisneros

items.title: Evaluating a Lightweight Neural Network for Aggregate Isotope Distribution Prediction
items.abstract: Isotope distribution prediction is an important part of mass spectrometry data analysis. A variety of strategies have been developed, including brute-force polynomial methods and Fourier-transform (FT) convolution methods. Here, we present a novel neural network (NN) approach to isotope prediction. These NN-based tools are distributed in a new package, IsoGen, alongside FT-based tools. We show that NNs perform as well as existing approaches when predicting isotope distributions for molecules with natural isotope ratios. We then demonstrate the capability of NNs for transfer learning, a method by which existing models that have been trained to perform one task can be reused as a starting point to train models to perform a second task. Here, a NN that has been trained to predict isotope distributions for molecules with natural isotope ratios can be retrained to predict distributions for molecules with perturbed isotope ratios. We also demonstrate that these training distributions do not need to be produced theoretically but may be extracted from experimental data where the underlying isotopic composition is not known. Overall, NNs provide a robust method for isotope prediction that can be extended to applications where the isotope distributions can be measured but not easily predefined.
items.authors: John G. Pavek, Josiah Grimes, Brian L. Frey, Nathan V. Welham, Lloyd M. Smith, Michael T. Marty

items.title: Visible-light-driven C2-phosphonylation of tryptophan in peptides and proteins
items.abstract: Tryptophan (Trp) residues are comparatively rare in proteins but are frequently positioned at sites that control folding, molecular recognition, ligand binding, and enzymatic activity. Direct chemical modification of Trp therefore offers a powerful strategy for perturbing protein structure and function. However, methods for installing compact, highly polar functionality onto native Trp residues under mild, protein-compatible conditions remain limited. Here we report a visible-light-driven reductive platform for the C2-selective phosphonylation of Trp-containing peptides and proteins using oxime phosphonates as radical precursors. The reaction proceeds under mild conditions, tolerates diverse peptide sequences containing nearly all proteinogenic amino-acid side chains, and enables late-stage modification of Trp-containing synthetic peptides or peptides derived from structurally complex bioactive molecules. The method further extends to native proteins in aqueous buffer, with LC-MS/MS analysis confirming site-selective modification across a range of protein substrates. Collectively, these results establish photochemical Trp-phosphonylation as a versatile method for peptide diversification, protein conjugation, and chemical control of biomolecular function in situ.
items.authors: Ranran Zhu, Xiaofei Gao, Xiaoying Lian, Diqi Yan, Fulai Li, Daokuan Sun

items.title: Photosensitive Phenothiazine-Fused [4]Helicenes
items.abstract: Here, we report the synthesis and photoreactivity of a phenothiazine fused [4]helicene, namely 3,13dimethoxybenzo[4,5]quinolino[3,2,1-kl]phenothiazine (MBQP). Comprehensive photophysical studies reveal that MBQP exhibits a high photoluminescence quantum yield of 60.3% and strong circularly-polarized luminescence, with high glum of 2.0 × 10-3 in DMSO. Besides its excellent chiroptical properties, MBQP can undergo a photoinduced chloroformylation reaction upon 365 nm irradiation in chloroform, enabling direct functionalization of the helicene framework. Notably, the emission of resulting photoproducts redshift to ~500, 550, and 660 nm, together with quantum yields up to 77.2%, demonstrating that the photochemical transformation can simultaneously functionalize the helicene framework and improve its luminescence performance. This work provides a straightforward example for the facile synthesis and post-functionalization of color-tunable chiral materials.
items.authors: Ling-Xiao Li, Gaoqiang Xu, Yue Zhang, Yonghong Xiao, Guiyi Yang, Yanning Xu

items.title: Chemoenzymatic synthesis of (E,E,Z)-humulene derived natural products
items.abstract: Among the 300 skeletally distinct products derived from farnesyl pyrophosphate (FPP) reported to date, meroterpenoids derived from the humulene core are of great interest due to their potent biological activities. Whereas the most available (E,E,E)-humulene core and derivatives thereof have been well-studied, comparatively little is known of the chemistry and biological properties of the related (E,E,Z)-core and natural products derived from this humulene isomer. Herein, we detail the first synthesis of (E,E,Z)-(10S)-hydroxyhumulene and elaborate this macrocycle through a chemoenzymatic route to (±)-deoxyeupenifeldin and neosetophomone B, and further accomplish the chemical synthesis of pughiinin A. The (E,E,Z)-(10S)-hydroxyhumulene was accessed via a selective oxidative double-bond isomerization from the (E,E,E)-humulene core. Additionally, when studying this macrocycle in subsequent hetero-Diels Alder (hDA) cycloadditions, it was observed that the (E,E,Z)-core imparted more biased diastereoselectivity when compared to previous studies of the corresponding (E,E,E)-core. Our findings demonstrate scalable access to (E,E,Z)-(10S)-hydroxyhumulene and the ability to build meroterpene natural products from this humulene isomer.
items.authors: Anthony Saucedo, Brian Valladares, David Delgadillo, Hosea Neslon, Alison Narayan

items.title: Programmable Oxidation in Flow on Interdigitated Lateral Catalytic Condensers
items.abstract: Heterogeneous catalysis remains fundamentally limited by the intrinsic static electronic and physical structure of the catalyst surface during reaction that restricts catalytic rates and limits reactions to equilibrium. To circumvent these limitations, a catalytic condenser enables the non-Faradaic dynamic modulation of surface binding energies through an external potential. Here, we describe an interdigitated (IDT) internal ion gel catalytic condenser within a continuous flow reactor for the electronic control of thermochemical carbon monoxide oxidation on Pt active sites. The device utilizes a thermally stable, high-capacitance ion gel electrolyte (PA6,6/[EDMIM][TFSI]) to establish an electric double layer at the metal-electrolyte interface, enabling both charge condensation and a strong electric field at the Pt active sites. Field strength was measured by Stark tuning of 4-mercaptobenzonitrile (4-MBN) on a model Ag electrode, with field strengths on the order of ~1 V nm -1 shifting a voltage-dependent nitrile response up to ~4 cm -1 /V at negative applied potential. By applying a bias of ±1 V at 180°C, the device both increases and decreases the catalytic turnover frequency of CO oxidation. These results support surface-charge modulation as the origin of catalytic rate enhancement for the non-Faradaic dynamic tuning of thermochemical reaction rates.
items.authors: Ruixue Xiong, Wonwoo Lee, Chaehoon Kim, Justin Hopkins, Jesse Canavan, Jaeheon Kim

items.title: Screening Natural and Modified Nucleobases to Create Alkylation-Resistant Nucleic Acids Toward Sensing Applications
items.abstract: Alkylating agents play critical roles in medicine and chemical defense but also pose significant hazards by modifying DNA and disrupting cellular function. Their reliable detection is therefore critical, yet current analytical methods are often limited by poor selectivity, need for extensive sample preparation, or poor compatibility with complex matrices. Nucleic acid sensors, such as aptamers, offer a promising route to achieve selective sensing. However, alkylation of nucleobases can compromise DNA three-dimensional structure and binding abilities. To address this limitation, we sought to develop DNA sequences that are resistant to alkylation. We first evaluated the reactivity of modified nucleobases toward a panel of alkylating agents. Although the N7 position 2 of guanosine and N3 position of adenosine have been reported to be among the primary alkylation sites, their analogues 7-deaza-2′-deoxyguanosine and 3-deaza-2′-deoxyadensoine were still found to be reactive. In contrast, 7-deaza-2′-deoxyinosine and 7-deaza-2′-deoxyadenosine were resistant to all alkylating agents tested. Using these resistant nucleobases as substitutes for all guanosine and adenosine residues, respectively, we screened polymerases and found that Therminator DNA Polymerase enabled enzymatic synthesis of fully alkylation-resistant DNA. This work establishes a chemical framework for the development of robust, DNA-based sensors for alkylating agents in biomedical and defense applications.
items.authors: Olamilekan Joseph Ibukun, Makenzie R. Walk, Jennifer M. Heemstra

items.title: From Silicon to Carbon: Experimental Validation of Generative AI-Derived CNS Drug Candidates — A Systematic Review (2021–2026)
items.abstract: Background Generative artificial intelligence has gained traction as an approach for designing novel CNS-relevant drug candidates, yet the extent to which computationally generated molecules undergo experimental validation remains poorly characterised. Methods A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines using a prospectively registered protocol (OSF: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/JE2DY). PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, arXiv, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched to March 2026. Eligible studies applied generative AI approaches to CNS-relevant targets and reported experimental wet laboratory validation. Titles and abstracts were screened independently by three reviewers; full-text screening, extraction, and quality appraisal were performed independently in duplicate. Findings were synthesised narratively; no meta-analysis was performed. Results Six studies met the inclusion criteria from 374 identified records. All performed in vitro validation; two additionally provided in vivo evidence. Despite CNS-focused objectives, one of six experimentally validated blood–brain barrier permeability. Three studies confirmed their primary computational predictions experimentally, whereas three showed partial confirmation. Validation rates, calculated as confirmed active compounds divided by compounds tested, ranged from 26 to 100 percent; these rates reflect differing selection stringency and are not directly comparable. Publicly accessible code was unavailable in four of six studies. Conclusions Among studies reaching experimental validation, blood–brain barrier confirmation, in vivo evidence, and code availability remain the exception. Because eligibility required reported validation, these findings describe successful translations and cannot estimate failure rates; they nonetheless indicate that validation depth, rather than molecular generation, is the current constraint in this field.
items.authors: Jad Awwad, Gul e Sehar, Fiona Benny, Obert Mutumba, Sukanya Mondal, Esha Shahbaz

items.title: Domino and Cascade Reactions in Sustainable Synthesis: Activation Modes, Assessment Boundaries, and the Molecular-Process Discrepancy
items.abstract: Domino and cascade reactions construct molecular complexity through sequential transformations and can reduce intermediate isolation. Their contribution to sustainable synthesis depends on whether these advantages persist when precursor preparation, catalyst production, reaction operation, and product recovery are included. This targeted narrative review examines thirteen mechanistic examples across seven activation or propagation modes and develops the molecular-process discrepancy (MPD) as a framework for testing that translation. MPD connects a specific reaction-level claim to the additional material and energy requirements introduced by expanding the assessment boundary. It complements atom economy, process mass intensity, E-factor, life-cycle assessment, and process benchmarks without replacing their measurements. Four case studies distinguish the roles of feedstock and product recovery in Ambrox synthesis, oxidant substitution in coumestan formation, advanced-substrate preparation in lasalocid A biosynthesis, and operational consolidation in oseltamivir synthesis. Together, they show why atom conservation, selective ring construction, and fewer isolations provide different forms of efficiency that must be evaluated separately. The analysis identifies precursor access, dilution, separation, catalyst lifetime, and heat, light, or oxygen delivery as specific targets for process improvement. MPD provides a procedure for determining whether a proposed cascade advantage is retained, attenuated, reversed, or unresolved across explicit assessment boundaries.
items.authors: Khang T. Hoa

items.title: A Library of Iron and α-Ketoglutarate Dependent Dioxygenases Enables the Synthesis of Six Fungal Natural Products
items.abstract: Achieving selective oxygenation chemistry offers a powerful strategy for streamlining routes to complex target molecules, yet the development of site-selective C-H functionalization reactions remain a significant challenge. Several enzyme families are capable of catalyzing C-H hydroxylation reactions and, in principle, provide an attractive solution for achieving selective oxidative transformations. In practice, however, the difficulty of identifying a biocatalyst suited to a specific synthetic target often renders chemoenzymatic strategies impractical. For example, biosynthetic enzymes such as CitB and ClaD can mediate site-selective benzylic hydroxylation, enabling access to select natural products that share structural features with their native substrates. Nonetheless, such approaches typically lack generality and do not readily extend to broader collections of natural products. Here, we explore the previously unstudied natural sequence space of the hydroxylases CitB and ClaD to generate a bespoke panel of uncharacterized enzymes that collectively expand the scope of this chemoenzymatic strategy. Development of this curated biocatalyst panel enabled the synthesis of six natural products, demonstrating that assembling this enzyme collection effectively derisks the use of biocatalysis in synthetic campaigns.
items.authors: Gonzalo J Villegas Rodríguez, Evan O Romero, Jonathan C Perkins, Diego N Rojas, Maximilian S Hrigora, Alison R H Narayan

items.title: Benchmark Label Definition, Not Model Capability, Explains a Machine-Learning Advantage over TD-DFT for λmax Prediction
items.abstract: Machine-learning models trained on literature-mined UV-Vis data are frequently reported to outperform time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) for predicting absorption maxima (λ max ). Such comparisons usually evaluate the model on held-out molecules from the same corpus that supplied its training labels, and they set experimental labels of heterogeneous transition type against computed vertical excitations of a single electronic transition. Using a Gaussian process (GP) with 256-bit Morgan fingerprints, trained on 6,878 curated compounds from the Beard literature-mined database, the study shows that two features of the benchmark, rather than model capability, govern the reported margin. On leakage-free in-corpus holdouts the GP outperforms the quantum-chemical references (RMSE 87.3 vs 108.7 nm against TD-DFT, n = 36; 81.6 vs 117.1 nm against sTDA, n = 1,011), and the advantage survives Bemis–Murcko scaffold splitting. Applied unchanged to genuinely external corpora, the same model keeps working where the label convention is compatible with training (R² = +0.209 on 5,811 compounds) and fails where it is not (R² = −0.269 with a +53.5 nm offset on 318 photoswitches labelled specifically to the E -isomer π→π* transition); chemical novelty alone does not break it, reassigning the label does. Against published ωB97X-D3 vertical excitations on 5,501 training-disjoint compounds, the calculations are the more accurate predictor once each method’s removable offset is discounted (≈58 vs 95 nm residual scatter) and correlate with experiment nearly twice as strongly (r = 0.85 vs 0.46). On the transition-specific corpus, CAM-B3LYP/6-31G** reaches 25.4 nm against the GP’s 80.9 nm. The 57–65 nm quantum-chemical underestimation seen in-corpus reappears out of sample at −61.9 nm against independently computed values, supporting a definitional rather than a functional origin. GP predictive uncertainty is poorly calibrated in all external regimes and does not reliably identify high-error predictions; its apparent correlation with error reflects the label variance of the evaluation set rather than structural distance from the training distribution. For this model class, reported margins over quantum chemistry should therefore be regarded as properties of the benchmark—its label definition and its same-corpus provenance,not of the method, unless the benchmark is external and its label convention is stated.
items.authors: Md Sahanawaz

items.title: Zirconium Oxynitride for the Oxygen Evolution Reaction
items.abstract: Zirconium oxynitride (Zr2ON2) has been proposed as a support material for iridium-lean oxygen evolution reaction (OER) catalysts, with Zr2ON2 representing a middle ground between conductive but readily oxidized ZrN and acid-stable but insulating ZrO2. Using density functional theory (DFT), we assess the stability of Zr2ON2 under operating conditions and consider it as a host for singleatom Ir catalysts. Substituting Ir into the Zr2ON2(111) surface creates active sites with theoretical OER overpotentials as low as 0.31 V, aided by a stabilization of the OOH∗ intermediate. Although Zr2ON2 is stable, or at worst marginally metastable, on the Zr–N–O convex hull, computational Pourbaix analysis shows it to be unstable in aqueous environments across pH and potential. These conditions drive N to leave as N2 or as dissolved species, leaving behind either dissolved Zr or ZrO2. Previously reported stable operation of Zr2ON2-based electrodes may therefore be reconciled with a self-passivating ZrO2 surface layer.
items.authors: Mathias Stokkebye Nissen, Christodoulos Chatzichristodoulou, Yang Hu, Heine Anton Hansen

items.title: Temperature-and pressure-dependent water stabilization of CO dimerization on Cu(100)
items.abstract: The electrochemical CO(2) reduction reaction offers a pathway to producing fuels and high-value chemicals from waste CO2 using renewable electricity. Among known catalysts, only copper in aqueous electrolytes enables the formation of C2+ products with high activity. The process of the C-C coupling is believed to be limited by the dimerization of two adsorbed *CO to form a *OC-CO* intermediate. Experimental strategies to improve selectivity toward C2+ products have recently focused on increasing temperature and pressure in the system, but the origins of these effects remain poorly understood. In this work, the thermodynamic and kinetic stability of the *OC-CO* dimer at the electrochemical interface of Cu(100) has been investigated, as a function of temperature and pressure using machine-learning interatomic potentials trained on DFT data. Extended molecular dynamics simulations with an explicit aqueous interface show that increased water density stabilizes the *OC-CO* intermediate through increased hydrogen bonding between interfacial water and the dimer. In contrast, temperature has no direct effect on the CO–CO association barrier, but instead indirectly influences reactivity by destabilizing *CO adsorption. Introducing a potassium cation leads to a large reduction in the interface work function, but only minor changes were observed in the energetics of the dimer formation. No correlation between cation-dimer distance and energetics is observed, suggesting a limited role of local field effects. These results identify hydrogen bonding as the key factor governing the stabilization of the *OC-CO* intermediate under experimental conditions. This work demonstrates how machine-learning interatomic potentials can facilitate systematic analysis of dynamic interfaces, and can be a powerful tool in theoretical exploration of electrolyte effects on reaction intermediates across extended time and length scales.
items.authors: Alberte H. Høholdt, Alexander Bagger, Alberte Holm Høholdt

items.title: ChiroptMap: Orbital-Cube-Free Transition-Moment Density Maps from Gaussian and ORCA
items.abstract: Earlier cube-based workflows generated electric-and magnetic-dipole transition-moment maps from molecular-orbital cubes exported with Gaussian cubegen from formatted-checkpoint data. ChiroptMap instead evaluates canonical orbitals and analytical derivatives blockwise from Gaussian WFX or an ORCA output/JSON/WFX bridge, eliminating intermediate orbital cubes while retaining final visualization cubes and S1–S6 CPL CSV values. Across ten Gaussian S1 TDA/TD-DFT cases, the median MDTM norm discrepancy decreased from 1.214% to 0.0541%, whereas EDTM recovery was unchanged; five S1/TDA cross-engine benchmarks gave mean field differences of 1.061% (electric) and 1.774% (magnetic), and the retained footprint decreased by 99.17%. Independent coefficient-print and spatial-grid tests support IOp(9/40=4) for the tested state while requiring both sources of numerical convergence to be assessed.
items.authors: Yuuya Nagata, Takashi Hirose

items.title: Deriving New Model Hamiltonians for [2Fe-2S] Iron-Sulfur Clusters
items.abstract: Iron–sulfur clusters are common bioinorganic cofactors found in many enzymes. Their open-shell electronic structures, characterized by strongly interacting d-electrons and a dense manifold of near-degenerate electronic states, often require computationally expensive multiconfigurational ab initio methods for their accurate treatment. Therefore, model Hamiltonians using a limited number of physically meaningful parameters are often used to describe their electronic structure properties. The Heisenberg-Dirac-Van Vleck Hamiltonian and the canonical Heisenberg double exchange model, which have traditionally been used to describe the electronic spectra of iron–sulfur clusters, can describe the lowest-energy state of each spin multiplicity. However, these models are limited to a relatively small set of spin degrees of freedom and cannot describe the full range of low-energy electronic excitations and therefore are not sufficient to reproduce the complete low-energy electronic spectrum. This motivates the development of more general model Hamiltonians for these systems. In this work, we employ the density matrix downfolding (DMD) method to derive an improved model Hamiltonian for the [Fe 2 S 2 (SCH 3 ) 4 ] 2-/3- cluster, which serve as models of the active site of ferredoxins containing the [2Fe–2S] motif. A generalized Hubbard-like Hamiltonian derived using DMD provides a substantially improved description of the low-energy spectrum using a relatively small number of physically meaningful parameters. Our matching pursuit analysis further shows that the exchange coupling parameter is selected only at a late stage of the optimization, while most of the exchange interaction is captured by the hopping and electron-electron interaction terms.
items.authors: Wyatt A. Gibbs, David Wilian Oliveira de Sousa, Elvira R. Sayfutyarova

items.title: Chemistry-Informed Multimodal Model for Structure Elucidation in Automated Reaction Discovery
items.abstract: Rapid and reliable structure elucidation remains a central bottleneck in automated reaction discovery, where highthroughput experimentation can generate large numbers of crude reaction mixtures faster than they can be interpreted. Gas chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry (GC-MS) provides rapid and information-rich analytical data, but identification of unknown reaction products still relies heavily on expert interpretation or spectral library matching, limiting applicability to novel compounds. Here we introduce Dynamic Mass-Aware Identification from Reaction Knowledge (DynaMAIK), a multimodal transformer framework for reaction-aware structure elucidation from GC-MS data. DynaMAIK combines electron ionization mass spectra with reaction context encoded as reactant and reagent SMILES to predict product structures and molecular formulas. Trained on more than three million reaction–spectrum pairs derived from curated reaction databases, spectral simulation and experimental spectra, DynaMAIK achieved 87% top-1 and 94% top-10 structure accuracy on a held-out experimental test set. Comparisons with spectrum-only and reaction-only models, together with ablation and scrambling experiments, show that spectral evidence and reaction-derived context provide complementary constraints for product identification. Application to high-throughput thiolation reactions demonstrates accurate product assignment directly from experimental screening data. DynaMAIK establishes context-aware GC-MS interpretation as a scalable route toward automated analytical feedback in reaction discovery workflows.
items.authors: Maik G. Niedziella, Philipp M. Pflüger, Ajnabiul Hoque, Frank Glorius

items.title: Beyond Recognition Chemistry: Ion Sensing through Intrinsic Electrochemical InterfacialResponse
items.abstract: Reliable ion sensing across multicomponent and dynamically changing environments is important in environmental monitoring, industrial process control, and biological analysis. In conventional electrochemical sensors, ion selectivity is typically achieved through redox reactions, ion-selective membranes, or molecular recognition layers, requiring ion-specific chemistry or materials to distinguish the target species. Yet dissolved ions also modify the intrinsic electrical structure of the electrode–electrolyte interface through differences in valence, hydrated size, mobility, polarizability, hydration energetics, and ion–surface interactions. These effects alter solvent organization, charge screening, ion accumulation, dielectric response, and transport within the electric double layer, creating composition-dependent electrical signatures without deliberately introduced receptors. Exploiting these intrinsic responses therefore offers an alternative basis for extracting ion-specific information from the interface itself. This review critically examines recognition-free ion sensing based on such intrinsic interfacial processes, with particular emphasis on non-Faradaic approaches. We first establish the physical origins of ion-dependent interfacial structure and examine how these differences are translated into measurable electrical responses, including capacitance, impedance, electronic channel modulation, ionic transport, and electrokinetic signals. The evolution of recognition-free sensing is then evaluated according to increasing analytical capability, from ion-dependent response and discrimination to single-analyte and multicomponent quantification. This analysis reveals that quantitative capability has advanced substantially, particularly through multidimensional electrical measurements and machine learning, but remains concentrated largely in simple solutions and controlled mixtures. Translation to complex and real matrices therefore represents a major unresolved frontier. Future progress will require deeper understanding of competitive multicomponent interfaces, deliberate control of interfacial properties, informative perturbation of the sensing environment, and data-driven analysis that remains connected to underlying physicochemical processes. Recognition-free sensing thus provides a route toward quantitative ion analysis in which analytical information is encoded by the interface itself rather than imposed exclusively through molecular recognition chemistry.
items.authors: Amir Mohseni Armaki, M. Ahmadi, A. Mol, P. Taheri, Amir Mohseni Armaki

items.title: Fully Deuterated [9]Cycloparaphenylene: Vibrational Modulation for Enhanced Solid-State Fluorescence
items.abstract: Fully deuterated [9]cycloparaphenylene ([9]CPP- d 36 ) was synthesized by gold-mediated macrocyclization. Although the molecular geometry and π-electronic structure of [9]CPP were retained, the framework vibrational frequencies were lowered. Solid-state [9]CPP- d 36 showed a higher fluorescence quantum yield than [9]CPP (0.46 vs 0.34), demonstrating H/D substitution as a vibrational-modulation approach for enhancing nanohoop fluorescence.
items.authors: Kenshiro Kusumi, Masaya Sugiura, Hidetoshi Kawai, Yoshitaka Tsuchido

items.title: Stage-Defined Prenyltransferase Integration for Hybrid RiPP Biosynthesis
items.abstract: Combining biosynthetic enzymes from distinct ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptide (RiPP) families offers a route to hybrid RiPPs but poses challenges in coordinating noncognate enzymatic transformations. Here, leveraging the temporal control enabled by in vitro biosynthesis, we first explored stage-defined integration of a cyanobactin prenyltransferase (PTase) into thiopeptide biosynthesis, a highly coordinated multienzyme pathway involving interdependent transformations of a single precursor peptide. Whereas early- and intermediate-stage prenylation interfered with thiopeptide maturation, late-stage prenylation of fully matured thiopeptides proceeded efficiently, enabling the production of diverse prenylated thiopeptides. We then extended this late-stage strategy to structurally distinct RiPPs, nonribosomal peptides, and artificial cyclic peptides using multiple cyanobactin PTases. Stage-controlled integration of non-cognate tailoring enzymes thus provides access to hybrid peptidic natural products.
items.authors: Sota Uchida, Taro Shiraishi, Marin Yokomine, Julien Alessandro König, Zhong Hui Lim, Dora Racunica

items.title: Self-Salting Coacervates: Interfacial Tension Reveals a Critical-Like Self-Suppression of Complex Coacervation
items.abstract: Complex coacervation is typically controlled via salt concentration, while the role of polymer concentration itself has received much less attention. Here, we show that increasing polyelectrolyte concentration can progressively suppress complex coacervation in a charge-stoichiometric, salt- free PDADMAC/PANa system. As polymer concentration increases, the coacervate phase swells while the polymer recovery stays nearly constant, and the compositions and densities of the coacervate and supernatant phases progressively converge. At = 400 mM, the macroscopic phase boundary vanishes and the system reaches a homogeneous, self-suppressed coacervation state. Over this range, the liquid–liquid interfacial tension decreases continuously toward zero following a critical-like power law with an exponent of 1.43 ± 0.03, close to the classical mean-field value of 3/2. These results show that polymer concentration is not merely a compositional variable, but can itself drive coacervation toward a critical-like, one-phase state by increasing salt-like screening from polymer-derived counterions, analogous to the effect of added salt.
items.authors: Yue Yu, Hongwei Li, Christophe Schatz, Jean-Paul Chapel

items.title: A traceable agentic framework for chemistry research query and analysis with ThermoML database
items.abstract: Reliable use of thermophysical databases in exploratory chemistry requires resolving heterogeneous identifiers, reconciling experimental conditions, and preserving numerical provenance across large, nested records. We present a hierarchical large language model (LLM) agent framework, implemented with a custom ReAct reasoning engine, that translates naturallanguage research questions into traceable retrieval and analysis workflows over the NIST ThermoML database. The framework combines hierarchical canonical identifiers, queryconditioned evidence compaction, deterministic inspection ledgers and numerical-grounding gates, and tool-assisted Redlich–Kister fitting. Five case studies are discussed in detail, representing chemistry tasks spanning data-rich and data-sparse retrieval, binary-mixture correlation, and open-ended cosolvent screening. For an ethanol–water equimolar density query, the system reduced ~190k characters of search output to 2k and precisely recovered a measured density of 859.3 kg m-3 at an ethanol mole fraction of 0.498, 298.15 K, and 100 kPa. For methanolethanol viscosity, it selected condition-aligned mixture and pure-component records, examined the fitting results at different orders, and produced a 2nd-order Redlich–Kister fit with 𝑅 = 0.982. Results for an open-ended iron-electrodeposition electrolyte design query synthesized evidence from approximately 12k measurements across 200 data blocks. However, with numerical grounding disabled for this specific case, the answer contained severe numerical hallucinations despite qualitatively coherent reasoning. These cases establish the feasibility of agent-assisted ThermoML research and identify identity management, evidence compaction, and deterministic numerical provenance as central design requirements for reliable chemistry-database research agents with some level of abstraction chemistry reasoning.
items.authors: Yunkai Sun, Adwaith Ravichandran, Hassan Harb, Rajeev S. Assary, Brian J. Ingram, Zhenzhen Yang

items.title: Investigation of α-Silylalcohols as Chiral Umpolung Carbanion Surrogates through Stereospecific 1,2-Brook Rearrangement
items.abstract: We report the investigation of the enantiospecific trapping of chiral α-silyl secondary alcohols through stereospecific 1,2-Brook rearrangement of the lithium alkoxide. The reaction proceeds through a chiral polarityreversed carbanion intermediate that can be trapped faster than racemization in many cases. Weinreb amides were applied as electrophile to access enantioenriched α-hydroxyketones in good yields and variable enantiopurities. Substituent effect studies showed that product enantiopurity was a function of the rate of electrophilic trapping of the intermediate chiral carbanion with faster trapping rates affording higher chirality transfer. The chiral α-silyl secondary alcohols were conveniently accessed in high enantiopurity using Noyori asymmetric transfer hydrogenation (ATH) with low catalyst loading (0.5 mol % Ru).
items.authors: TyAnn McHenry, Joshua D. Sieber

items.title: The infinitesimal surgeon: nanomachines and upconversion nanoparticles
items.abstract: The concept of the infinitesimal machine surgeon: a tiny nano-sized machine with moving parts “akin to a little knife”; which is guided to a biological target; and which is human controlled via an electromagnetic input; was loosely envisaged by Feynman two influential lectures in 1959 and 1983. In this perspective, we examine how chemistry – not physics - may be on the cusp on creating a true infinitesimal machine surgeon. We extract four key criteria for an infinitesimal machine surgeon. We set out how nanomachines – light activated molecular rotors – can trigger cell death via mechanical action, and highlight the recently demonstrated combination of nanomachines and photonic upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs), which enable control of nanomachines with near-infrared (NIR) light. This advancement conceivably enables the ability to control nanomachines in deep tissue ( 1 cm) using diffuse NIR illumination, surpassing depth limits of conventional and two photon excitation (2PE) of nanomachines. We set out directions for future development of nanomachines and UCNPs, for deep-tissue applications, including opportunities for targeted delivery and multi-modal tracking. With sufficient development, we expect the conjunction of UCNPs and nanomachines can fulfil all four criteria to be considered an infinitesimal machine surgeon.
items.authors: Lewis E. MacKenzie

items.title: Terminal 4-Cyanophenyl Functionalization of Helical Nanographenes: Mechanistic Insights into Columnar Assembly and Near-Infrared Chiroptical Modulation
items.abstract: We report a primary helical nanographene terminally functionalized with 4-cyanophenyl groups. This terminal substitution dictates columnar solid-state assembly and selectively stabilizes frontier orbitals deriving narrow HOMO–LUMO gap. It also induces redshifted absorption and amplifies circular dichroism via transition moment density redistribution, providing rational design principles for helical π-systems.
items.authors: Zhibo Liu, Takashi Hirose

items.title: Formation of the titanium oxyl at an electrochemical interface: limiting the role of solvent re-orientation in strong electric fields
items.abstract: The oxidation of water at surfaces requires reactive and metastable intermediates such as surface adsorbed and often electron deficient oxygen. An outstanding question is whether forming these intermediates depends primarily on the energetics of adsorption associated with the reorganization of bonds at a vacuum interface, or whether it must include contributions from the re-orientation of water dipoles and ions within the aqueous electrolyte that could lower the free energy. Time-resolved mid-infrared experiments in an attenuated total reflection geometry have detected the terminal oxygen, the titanium oxyl, by a vibration that forms underneath it. The vibration was shown to couple to the librational modes of water by a Fano resonance. Here, we show that the picosecond formation of the titanium oxyl’s vibration is invariant across interfaces that change the density of librational modes (air, pH 7, pH 13, and pD 13), as detected by significant modifications of the coupled line-shape. Across the interfaces, we report a common rate constant (0.56 +/- 0.08 ps) and half rise (1.76 +/- 0.39 ps). This demonstrates that the reorganizational energy associated with solvent re-orientation is limited to affecting the ultrafast (400 fs) time resolution of the experiment characteristic of activation-less reactions and bond-reorganization. Furthermore, the formation kinetics are well-fit by a logistic function that describes an autocatalytic reaction and the surface population of titanium oxyl with excitation is well modelled by the Langevin equation. Both suggest that the invariant picosecond rise is due to a re-orientation of the titanium oxyl and its p-polarized vibrational dipole with respect to the strong Helmholtz electric field common to the probed interfaces.
items.authors: Paul Zayka, James Stewart, Tanja Cuk

items.title: Synthesizing N-indole Carbamates via CO2 Valorization in o-difluorobenzene driven by pKa Values of N-H Covalent Bonds
items.abstract: A green synthetic route for accessing N -indole carbamates, a key building block of bioactive molecules, can be achieved using indole and CO 2 . However, using strong bases results in low yields and reduced functional group tolerance, making it more challenging to develop milder reactions. The proton transfer from indole N-H bond to base is one of the essential steps in synthesizing N-indole carbamates, which is highly dependent on the driving force ΔG PT and their corresponding p K a values in the solution-state. In this study, the optimized condition was experimentally approved and driven by the ΔG PT values derived from the experimentally determined pKa values of 31 N–H covalent bonds in six polar fluorinated arenes, resulting in synthesizing N-indole carbamates in o-difluorobenzene promoted by MTBD via CO 2 valorization at room temperature, which is free of catalysts or additives and exhibits excellent functional group tolerance with moderate to excellent yields. Compared to commonly used organic solvents like THF and acetonitrile, the ΔG PT can be significantly reduced in o-difluorobenzene. And DFT analysis revealed that o-DFB can regulate the reaction mechanism through a pathway in which indole anionic intermediate formed before the activation of CO 2 .
items.authors: Xiangmei Kong, Tianxing Lin, Zhenbo Guo, Yunfei Liang, Shanhui Zhu, Qinbo Jiao

items.title: Intramolecular Alkene Protonation Enables Stereoconvergent Catalysis Through Tertiary Carbenium Ions
items.abstract: Enantioselective trapping of tertiary carbenium ions is often complicated by competing E1 elimination. Here, we show that a chiral oxazaborolidinium ion catalyst promotes ground-state intramolecular proton transfer from a phenolic OH group to an adjacent alkene, generating a catalyst-associated tertiary carbenium ion for enantioselective trapping. This activation mode allows alkenes formed by E1 elimination to regenerate reactive cations during the stereoconvergent conversion of racemic tertiary alcohols.
